Workflow artifact: ci-fix
Artifact kind: help
Refs: dotnet/maui#36453
Target branch: net11.0
Attempt: 1/10



## Attempt 1 of 10

Synchronize the picker crash regression test with its automatic navigation instead of sleeping for a fixed duration.

### Previous attempts (prior commits on this PR)

None; this is the first attempt.

This attempt differs by removing the fixed four-second delay and using the main-page automation elements as the completion condition. It does not increase a timeout, retry the test, or weaken its crash detection.

## Root cause

The test holds the MacCatalyst picker dialog open while the page automatically pops after three seconds, then waits a fixed four seconds. Fixed timing does not synchronize Appium with the navigation transition and can leave it querying the dismissed picker accessibility element, producing either a timeout or stale-element error.

## Fix

Remove the fixed sleep and immediately wait for the main page's `statusLabel` and `navigateButton`. Those waits poll through the automatic pop and complete only after navigation has made the expected page observable.

## What is unverified / where I need help

- MacCatalyst UI tests cannot run on this Linux runner.
- Please confirm `PickerDialogDoesNotCrashWhenPagePoppedWhileDialogOpen` passes on the MacCatalyst UI-test leg.

## Validation

- Command: `not run because MacCatalyst UI tests require a macOS runner`
- Result: not run

## Evidence

- Original failing build: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1498914
- Latest verified-failing build: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1498914

### Continuously build, test, and deploy to any platform and cloud

[Azure Pipelines](https://azure.microsoft.com/services/devops/pipelines/) offers cloud-hosted pipelines for Linux, macOS, and Windows with 10 free parallel jobs and unlimited minutes for open source projects.

:v: **Any language, platform, and cloud**
Build, test, and deploy Node.js, Python,  Java, PHP, Ruby, Go, C/C++, C#, Android, and iOS apps. Run in parallel on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Deploy to cloud providers like Azure, AWS, and GCP. Distribute mobile apps through beta channels and app stores.

:whale2: **Native container support**
Create new containers with ease and push them to any registry. Deploy containers to independent hosts or Kubernetes.

:muscle: **Advanced workflows and features**
Easy build chaining and multi-phased builds. Support for YAML, test integration, release gates, reporting, and more.

:wrench: **Extensible**
Use a range of build, test, and deployment tasks built by the community – hundreds of extensions from Slack to SonarCloud. You can even deploy from other CI systems, like Jenkins. Webhooks and REST APIs help you integrate.

:blue_heart: **Free, to you from Azure Pipelines**
Free cloud-hosted builds for public and private repositories.

[Content truncated due to length]
content.body:
## Summary
`PickerDialogDoesNotCrashWhenPagePoppedWhileDialogOpen` (Issue31731) consistently fails in the `Controls Page,Performance,Picker,ProgressBar` MacCatalyst UI test leg on `net11.0`, with either a `TimeoutException` (waiting for the `colorPicker` TextField element) or a `StaleElementReferenceException` (element no longer present after dialog close). Appears in 2 of the last 3 completed builds.

## Build Information
- **Pipeline**: maui-pr-uitests (ID 313)
- **Build**: [1498914](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1498914)
- **Build ID**: 1498914
- **Branch**: net11.0
- **First seen**: 2026-07-07 (build 1496867)
- **Occurrences**: 2 in last 3 builds (1498914, 1496867)

## Affected Legs
- `Controls Page,Performance,Picker,ProgressBar` — MacCatalyst UITests (CoreCLR)

## Error Message
```
Failed PickerDialogDoesNotCrashWhenPagePoppedWhileDialogOpen [30 s]
  Error Message:
   System.TimeoutException : Timed out waiting for element...
     at UITest.Appium.HelperExtensions.WaitForElement(...)
     at Microsoft.Maui.TestCases.Tests.Issues.Issue31731.PickerDialogDoesNotCrashWhenPagePoppedWhileDialogOpen()
       in src/Controls/tests/TestCases.Shared.Tests/Tests/Issues/Issue31731.cs:line 40

-- build 1496867 variant --
  OpenQA.Selenium.StaleElementReferenceException : The element "colorPicker" TextField identified by
  "EA0DA19F-..." is not present on the current view (No matches found for Elements matching predicate
  '"colorPicker" IN identifiers' from input {Window, Button, Group, Group}).
```

## Recommended Action
1. Open `src/Controls/tests/TestCases.Shared.Tests/Tests/Issues/Issue31731.cs` — the test opens a Picker dialog then pops the page; validate that the `colorPicker` element wait handles the case where the dialog/element is dismissed before the assertion.
2. Check if a `Picker` dialog dismiss / page pop race condition was introduced in recent `MacCatalyst` Picker handler changes (`src/Controls/src/Core/Handlers/Picker/`).
3. Add a guard / longer wait or verify the element is dismissed before asserting its absence to avoid `StaleElementReferenceException`.

pr.title: [ci-fix] Needs review: mark Apple runner interop as safe (refs #134061)
pr.body:
Workflow artifact: ci-fix
Artifact kind: help
Linked KBE: #134061

> [!NOTE]
> This is an AI/Copilot-generated **best-effort** fix attempt that I could not fully validate. It is a starting point for a maintainer, not a finished change. Please review the analysis below before merging.

## Root cause (best analysis)
Apple NativeAOT test legs fail to compile `AppleTestRunner.cs`: the source-generated `LibraryImport` declarations for `mono_ios_append_output` and `mono_ios_set_summary` trigger SYSLIB1064 because they lack an explicit memory-safety context.

## Attempted fix
Marks both P/Invoke declarations `safe`. They marshal managed strings and expose no pointer parameters, so this preserves the runner’s existing interop behavior while satisfying the compiler’s required explicit context.

## What is unverified / where I need help
- The required libraries baseline build could not be started because the execution environment rejected `./build.sh clr+libs -rc release` before execution.
- Please confirm this compiler-version-specific `safe` annotation is accepted across the Apple NativeAOT target matrix.

## Validation
- Command: `./build.sh clr+libs -rc release`
- Result: not run because the execution environment rejected the command before it started

## Evidence
- Failing build: [1596986](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1596986)
- First build it occurred: [1596986](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1596986) — 2026-09-15 UTC
- Suspected regressing change: none identified with sufficient confidence

- Area owners (`area-Infrastructure-libraries`): `@dotnet/area-infrastructure-libraries`

The GitHub Policy Service is created and maintained by the GitHub Inside Microsoft team at Microsoft 1ES. This service is the foundation for the compliance and governance efforts on our GitHub instances. In a nutshell, the Policy Service manages GitHub organizations and repositories using Config-As-Code.

This instance is dedicated to the .NET Foundation and its projects.

Microsoft project maintainers who are employees can learn more about this app, including support and feedback opportunities, at [GitOps](https://aka.ms/1es-gitops).
For commands to interact with the bots you have to use @dotnet-policy-service.

content.title: XHarness package install failure on iOS due to devicectl NSPOSIXErrorDomain error 49
content.body:
> **_Note:_** This issue was automatically generated by AI-Test-Triage. Please review and triage accordingly. ## Build Information Build: [20260128.103](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1271034), [20260129.5](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1272660), [20260129.80](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1272563) Build error leg or test failing: System.Runtime.Tests.WorkItemExecution, iOS.Device.ExportManagedSymbols.Test.WorkItemExecution, iOS.CoreCLR.Interpreter.Test.WorkItemExecution, iOS.CoreCLR.R2R.Test.WorkItemExecution, iOS.Device.Aot.Test.WorkItemExecution, Directed_2.WorkItemExecution, JIT.CodeGenBringUpTests_r.WorkItemExecution, Loader.WorkItemExecution, LoaderClassloaderRegressions.WorkItemExecution, Methodical_ro.WorkItemExecution, Regression_ro_1.WorkItemExecution, StackTraceMetadata.WorkItemExecution, DynamicGenerics.WorkItemExecution, Reflection.WorkItemExecution, TrimmingBehaviors.WorkItemExecution, JIT.Generics.WorkItemExecution, Regression_9.WorkItemExecution, reflection.WorkItemExecution Affected CI jobs: build_ios_arm64_Release_AllSubsets_Mono_Smoke, build_ios_arm64_Release_AllSubsets_CoreCLR_Smoke, build_iOS_arm64_Release_AllSubsets_Mono, build_ios_arm64_Release_AllSubsets_NativeAOT_Smoke, build_ios_arm64_Release_AllSubsets_Mono_RuntimeTests, build_ios_arm64_Release_AllSubsets_NativeAOT_RuntimeTests ### Causing Commit Range Information Commit range: {TODO: Insert commit range or link to changes} ## Summary - Package installation fails: mlaunch/devicectl exits with code 1 causing XHarness PACKAGE_INSTALLATION_FAILURE (exit code 78). - Observed on macOS hosts using Xcode 26.x and mlaunch/devicectl when deploying arm64 iOS device workloads across multiple jobs. - devicectl reports NSPOSIXErrorDomain error 49 ('Can't assign requested address'); devicectl JSON often shows tunnelState disconnected and tunnelIPAddress nil (tcp). - Both install and uninstall devicectl commands fail, preventing app removal and producing no xunit test results; XHarness saves diagnostics.json. - Logs show devicectl invoked with elevated privileges and warnings; comments.body:
I dug into several recent occurrences. This appears to be a physical-device pool health problem rather than a runtime or test failure.

The iPhone is successfully enumerated, but its CoreDevice connection is unusable: `usbmuxd` fails to connect to device port 62078, remote pairing resets, and `devicectl` cannot establish a tunnel or obtain a tunnel IP. Installation then fails with `NSPOSIXErrorDomain error 49` before any tests run.

Helix requests an infrastructure retry and host reboot, but unhealthy host/device pairs later return to the queue. For example, the same `System.Runtime.Tests` payload failed installation on `DNCENGMAC116`, retried on `DNCENGMAC123`, and then passed all 78,624 tests. This suggests the pool admission check verifies basic availability or device enumeration, but not a working CoreDevice tunnel.

The affected pairs should be quarantined until they pass an end-to-end health check that establishes the tunnel and performs a real `devicectl` install/uninstall. A host reboot alone does not appear sufficient.

> [!NOTE]
> This analysis was generated with GitHub Copilot.

> I dug into several recent occurrences. This appears to be a physical-device pool health problem rather than a runtime or test failure.

Yes, not sure why it keep repeating. I requested First Responders to restart the affected physical devices.

## Snapshot — 2026-10-03T14:33Z

content.title: [ci-scan-feedback] Read ci-fix head.ref via list_pull_requests to close fixer dedup gap
content.body:
## Triggering signals

- **#134186** (2026-09-18, `[ci-fix]` help-wanted) is a **byte-identical duplicate** of the already-open **#134134** (2026-09-17): same one-file diff (`src/libraries/Common/tests/AppleTestRunner/AppleTestRunner.cs`, mark two `LibraryImport` declarations `safe`), both `kind: help`, both `Linked KBE: #134061`, both on a `ci-fix/134061-` head branch. The fixer opened a second help-wanted PR for a KBE that already had an open `[ci-fix]` PR — a Step 3 dedup miss. https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/134186
- **#132616** (2026-08-21, still open, orphaned `[ci-scan-feedback]` issue) diagnosed this exact gap: `search_pull_requests` never returns `head.ref`, so the `ci-fix/<kbe>-` branch key that Step 3 relies on is invisible to search alone. Its PR failed to push and was never applied; the same failure mode has now reproduced. https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/132616
- **#134134** carries **no `Linked KBE:` body field** (its title is `[ci-fix] ... (refs #134061)`), so even the search fallback (body contains `Linked KBE: #<kbe>`) could not see it — the branch prefix was the only reliable key, and it was unreadable via search.

## Proposed edits

- `.github/workflows/ci-failure-fix.md` (Step 3 enumeration paragraph) — instruct the fixer to resolve open-candidate `[ci-fix]` head branches via `list_pull_requests` (which returns `head.ref`) and merged/closed candidates via `pull_request_read get`, because `search_pull_requests` omits `head.ref`; state that an empty branch map means "not yet enumerated", not "no open PR".

content.title: [ICC760][Extracción] Incorporar evidencia de issues vinculados a PRs cerrados sin merge (discrepancia A)
content.body:
## Para el agente de desarrollo que diseñó el pipeline ICC760

Implementa esta corrección **en el código y en la documentación**, respetando el diseño existente, el formato de los artefactos y la reproducibilidad del estudio ICC760. No cambies la definición de la muestra (PRs cerrados sin merge) ni presentes una issue mencionada como causa confirmada de cierre sin evidencia.

## Problema comprobado

El diseño metodológico contempla el examen de *issues vinculados* para contextualizar por qué un PR fue cerrado sin merge. Sin embargo, `ICC760/scripts/collect_pr_evidence.py` actualmente reúne el cuerpo del PR, comentarios, reviews, review comments y CI; **no recupera estructuradamente las issues relacionadas**. Un caso de la muestra piloto, [dotnet/runtime#134186](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/134186), usa la información de [dotnet/runtime#134305](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/134305) en `ICC760/analisis_cualitativo.csv`.

## Cambios solicitados

- [ ] Extiende `ICC760/scripts/collect_pr_evidence.py` con una etapa identificable de descubrimiento de issues relacionadas (por ejemplo, referencias verificables y/o eventos de timeline de GitHub). Documenta qué relaciones se admiten y sus limitaciones; **una mera mención textual no equivale automáticamente a causalidad**.
- [ ] Guarda en `ICC760/output/pr_evidence.json` un campo estructurado y estable para issues vinculadas: repositorio, número, URL, tipo/origen de relación, evidencia y, cuando esté disponible, contenido relevante. No dupliques una misma issue si aparece por varias vías.
- [ ] Maneja enlaces cruzados, repositorios distintos, permisos/404, paginación y fallos de API sin bloquear el procesamiento de otros PRs. Registra errores de recolección de manera trazable.
- [ ] Mantén la compatibilidad de los campos ya utilizados por la codificación cualitativa y el comportamiento reanudable de la extracción.
- [ ] Actualiza `ICC760/README.md` para dejar explícito qué información se recolecta automáticamente y qué consulta o interpretación sigue siendo manual; documenta el comando necesario para ejecutar esta etapa.
- [ ] Agrega pruebas con respuestas simuladas de GitHub: PR con issue relacionada, PR sin relación, relación duplicada, cruce de repositorios y error de API.

## Criterios de aceptación

1. Para `dotnet/runtime#134186`, el procedimiento permite identificar y documentar correctamente la relación verificable con `dotnet/runtime#134305` cuando GitHub la expone; si no hay relación recuperable automáticamente, lo consigna como limitación y preserva la revisión manual.
2. Para PRs sin referencias pertinentes, el campo estructurado queda vacío (no genera relaciones falsas).
3. El script puede reanudarse y sigue generando un JSON válido sin perder las evidencias anteriores.

pr.title: [repo-assist] docs: document known Debug-mode F# compiler bug affecting taskSeq (#473)
pr.body:
🤖 *This PR was created automatically by Repo Assist, an AI assistant. A human maintainer should review before merging.* ## What Adds a **Known issues** section to `README.md` documenting an upstream F# compiler regression discovered while investigating #473: Debug builds on recent .NET SDKs (`10.0.400`+ / F# 10+) can silently truncate a `taskSeq { }` sequence that `do!`/awaits between `yield`s. `MoveNextAsync` simply returns `false` after the first await — no exception, no warning. ## Root cause This is **not a bug in FSharp.Control.TaskSeq**: - It only reproduces in Debug (`-c Debug`) — Release (`-c Release` / `-p:Optimize=true`) always works correctly. - It is already tracked upstream as [dotnet/fsharp#20466](https://github.com/dotnet/fsharp/issues/20466) ("Incorrect state machine compilation in debug"), filed using this repo as the repro case. - A fix is already in progress at [dotnet/fsharp#20469](https://github.com/dotnet/fsharp/pull/20469), which matches how `TaskSeqBuilder.fs`'s `Bind`/`WhileAsync`/`For` compose `ResumableCode` values. Since this can't be fixed in library source (it's a compiler-lowering issue), documenting it clearly helps users hitting it (like the reporter of #473, whose tests silently passed on only the first item because `dotnet test` defaults to Debug) find a workaround quickly. ## Change - `README.md`: new "Known issues" section with a short description, links to the upstream issue/fix PR, and the workaround (build/test in Release). - `release-notes.txt`: added an `Unreleased` bullet per repo convention. ## Test Status Documentation-only change; no source code modified. `dotnet fantomas . --check` is not applicable (no `.fs`/`.fsx` files touched). No build or test run required per repo guidelines for docs-only changes. Relates to #473 (does not close it, since the root cause is external to this library). > Generated by 🌈 Repo Assist, see [workflow run](https://github.com/fsprojects/FSharp.Control.TaskSeq/actions/runs/35351883268). content.title: Incorrect state machine compilation in debug
content.body:
Please provide a succinct description of the issue.

**Repro steps**

1. Clone https://github.com/fsprojects/FSharp.Control.TaskSeq
2. just run smoke tests in VS test explorer or:
edit sdk pin in global.json to "10.0.400"
`dotnet test -c Debug .\src\FSharp.Control.TaskSeq.SmokeTests\`
builds fine, runs fine, taskSeq produces wrong values and tests fail.


This is particularly nasty, because it builds and runs, just the execution is wrong.

Tests pass up to sdk 10.0.204, fail for 10.0.400 and 11 preview.
content.author: majocha

comments.body: Large part of it is that TaskSeq's dynamic implementation is incomplete and untested. Up til recently we emitted the static implementation even in debug, so this was hidden and not exercised unless a consumer wrote code that did not statically compile.

`<OtherFlags>--always-inline+</OtherFlags>` should help in the meantime.

I would also love if we could have an addition to the regression testing matrix guarding `TaskSeq`.

content.title: taskSeq stops after the first await (Task.Yield/Task.Delay between yields) when the consuming project is built in Debug; Release works (TaskSeq 1.1.1, .NET SDK 10.0.400)
content.body:
## Summary

With `FSharp.Control.TaskSeq` 1.1.1, a `taskSeq` that awaits between yields (`do! Task.Yield()` or `do! Task.Delay n`) stops after the first await when the **consuming project is compiled in the Debug configuration**. The same code enumerates every item in Release. `TaskSeq.toListAsync`, a manual `GetAsyncEnumerator` / `MoveNextAsync` loop and an ASP.NET Core response writer consuming the `IAsyncEnumerable` are all affected. A `taskSeq` without awaits between yields is fine.

Impact: `dotnet test` builds Debug by default, so tests that stream through a `taskSeq` silently observe only the first item. That is how I ran into it (an xunit test of a chunked HTTP writer that takes an `IAsyncEnumerable`).

## Repro

`Repro.fsproj`

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <Compile Include="Program.fs" />
  </ItemGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="FSharp.Control.TaskSeq" Version="1.1.1" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

`Program.fs`

```fsharp
open System.Threading.Tasks
open FSharp.Control

let awaitBetweenYields () =
    taskSeq {
        yield 1
        do! Task.Yield()
        yield 2
        do! Task.Delay 5
        yield 3
    }

let delayOnly () =
    taskSeq {
        yield 1
        do! Task.Delay 5
        yield 2
    }

let forLoopWithDelay () =
    taskSeq {
        for i in 1..3 do
            do! Task.Delay 1
            yield i
    }

let noAwaits () =
    taskSeq {
        yield 1
        yield 2
        yield 3
    }

let manualEnumeration (source: taskSeq<int>) =
    task {
        let e = source.GetAsyncEnumerator()
        let results = ResizeArray()
        while! e.MoveNextAsync() do
            results.Add e.Current
        return List.ofSeq results
    }

printfn "awaitBetweenYields toListAsync : %A" (awaitBetweenYields() |> TaskSeq.toListAsync).Result
printfn "awaitBetweenYields manual loop : %A" (manualEnumeration(awaitBetweenYields())).Result
printfn "delayOnly          toListAsync : %A" (delayOnly() |> TaskSeq.toListAsync).Result
printfn "forLoopWithDelay   toListAsync : %A" (forLoopWithDelay() |> TaskSeq.toListAsync).Result
printfn "noAwaits           toListAsync : %A" (noAwaits() |> TaskSeq.toListAsync).Result
```

Output:

```
$ dotnet run -c Debug
awaitBetweenYields toListAsync : [1]
awaitBetweenYields manual loop : [1]
delayOnly          toListAsync : [1]
forLoopWithDelay   toListAsync : []
noAwaits           toListAsync : [1; 2; 3]

$ dotnet run -c Release
awaitBetweenYields toListAsync : [1; 2; 3]
awaitBetweenYields manual loop : [1; 2; 3]
delayOnly          toListAsync : [1; 2]
forLoopWithDelay   toListAsync : [1; 2; 3]
noAwaits           toListAsync : [1; 2; 3]
```

No exception is thrown; `MoveNextAsync` simply returns `false` after the first await.

## Environment

- Windows 11 (10.0.26200), x64
- .NET SDK 10.0.400, `net10.0`, FSharp.Core 10.1.400 (assembly 10.1.0.0, file version 10.104.26.38015)
- Also reproduces with .NET SDK 11.0.100-preview.6, `net11.0`, FSharp.Core 11.0.0.0 (file version 11.1.126.36018)
- FSharp.Control.TaskSeq 1.1.1

## What I could narrow down

- The `awaitBetweenYields` result is deterministic (3 of 3 runs each: Debug `[1]`, Release `[1; 2; 3]`). The `for` shape flips between `[]` and `[1]` across Debug runs, so a race looks likely.
- It is not the runtime or the dependencies: `bin/Debug` and `bin/Release` contain byte-identical `FSharp.Core.dll` and `FSharp.Control.TaskSeq.dll`, the `deps.json` files are identical and the `runtimeconfig.json` files differ only by `MetadataUpdater.IsSupported`. Copying the Release-compiled `Repro.dll` into the Debug output folder works; copying the Debug-compiled `Repro.dll` into the Release output folder fails. So it depends on how the consuming assembly (the one containing the `taskSeq { }` block) is compiled.
- The full `fsc` argument diff between the two configurations is only: Debug `--define:DEBUG --optimize- --tailcalls- -g` versus Release `--define:RELEASE --optimize+`.
- Building Release with the Debug flag set (`dotnet run -c Release -p:Optimize=false -p:Tailcalls=false -p:DebugSymbols=true -p:DebugType=portable -p:DefineConstants=DEBUG`) reproduces the bug. Building Debug with the Release flag set (`dotnet run -c Debug -p:Optimize=true -p:Tailcalls=true -p:DebugSymbols=false -p:DebugType=none -p:DefineConstants=RELEASE`) makes it work.
- Flipping a single flag was not enough for me: Debug with `-p:Optimize=true -p:Tailcalls=true` (still `-g`) fails, Release with `-p:Optimize=false -p:Tailcalls=false` (no `-g`) works, and Debug with `-p:DebugSymbols=false -p:DebugType=none` (still `--optimize-`) fails.
- The failing binaries carry `DebuggableAttribute(IsJITOptimizerDisabled = true)`; the working ones do not.

Happy to provide anything else that helps.

comments.body:
🤖 *This is an automated response from Repo Assist.* Thanks for the very thorough repro and diagnosis — this made root-causing straightforward! I reproduced this locally against both the published `1.1.1` NuGet package and the current `main` branch source, with .NET SDK `10.0.400`. Debug consistently drops everything after the first `do!`. This is **not a bug in FSharp.Control.TaskSeq** — it's an F# compiler regression in how the Debug-mode lowering handles resumable state machines that are *composed* across builder boundaries (i.e. `TaskSeq`'s use of `ResumableCode` combinators like `Bind`/`WhileAsync`/`For` calling into each other). It's already tracked upstream: - dotnet/fsharp#20466 — "Incorrect state machine compilation in debug" (filed against this exact repro) - dotnet/fsharp#20469 — fix PR, open as of this writing: *"Debug compilation could route inline builders containing low-level resumable state machines through generated helper methods. That helper boundary hid nested `ResumableCode` definitions from lowering, causing incorrect execution for composed builders such as `TaskSeq`."* That description matches exactly what's happening in `TaskSeqBuilder.fs`'s `Bind`/`WhileAsync`/`For` methods, which chain `ResumableCode` values together. **Workaround until the compiler fix ships**: build/test with `-p:Optimize=true` (or use a `-c Release` build) for any project that consumes `taskSeq { }` with awaits between yields. Since `dotnet test` defaults to Debug, CI/test projects relying on `taskSeq` may need `dotnet test -c Release` or an explicit `true` override in Debug until SDKs ship the compiler fix. No action is needed in this repo's source — this will self-resolve once the upstream fix lands in an SDK release. content.title: API docs: link postfix FSharp.Core type constructors (list, option, seq) in type signatures
content.body: ## Summary In API docs, postfix FSharp.Core type constructors such as `list`, `option`, `voption` and `seq` are rendered as plain text in type signatures, while other types get a link. For example the "Abbreviation For" line of [`MarkdownSpans`](https://fsprojects.github.io/FSharp.Formatting/reference/fsharp-formatting-markdown-markdownspans.html) renders as ```html MarkdownSpan list ``` `MarkdownSpan` is linked, `list` is not. It would be nice if `list` linked to https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-list-1.html, the way `FSharpList` already does when it shows up under its compiled name. The same applies wherever a type is formatted: member signatures, record fields, union case fields, return types. ## Cause `formatTyconRefAsHtml` in `src/FSharp.Formatting.ApiDocs/TypeFormatter.fs` calls `CrossReferenceResolver.TryResolveEntity` on the type constructor. For `int list` the type constructor reported by FSharp.Compiler.Service is FSharp.Core's `list<'T>` abbreviation entity (`IsFSharpAbbreviation = true`), not `FSharpList<'T>`. For that entity `TryFullName` is `None`, so `tryResolveCrossReferenceForEntity` returns `None` and the formatter falls back to plain text. Quick check with FCS 43.12.401 on `type B = int option`: ``` tcref=option IsFSharpAbbreviation=true TryFullName=None ``` ## Suggested fix In `tryResolveCrossReferenceForEntity`, when the entity is not registered and is an F# abbreviation with no full name, resolve the link through the abbreviated type's definition (`entity.AbbreviatedType.TypeDefinition`, here `FSharpList`1`) while keeping the abbreviation's display name (`list`) as the link text. `externalDocsLink` already maps `FSharpList` to the fsharp-core-docs URL above and `FSharpOption` to `option`, so only the entity lookup needs to change. Follow-up from #1314.

content.body: Hello, I have been trying to include visual content in library documentation. My use case is that I am working on a project that interfaces heavily with CAD workflows. So, it would be very valuable to be able to save snapshots of diagrams/drawings and include them in documentation that is then built into the static content by `fsdocs`. I first asked on the [fsharp slack](https://fsharp.slack.com/archives/C04BJKUP2/p1719339966559109) for advice on the topic. For example: ```fsharp /// Pi is the ratio of circle's circumference to its diameter. /// ![remote image](https://www.probability.ca/jeff/writing/pi1.jpg) /// /// ![local image](images/pi.png) let pi = 3.14159 ``` Would result in an HTML tag like `` (or some other path in the `output` directory) in the documentation for that value. It would be nice to be able to support embedded HTML, especially for resizing images. But I think supporting markdown images would be a good start if it is not already supported. I have tried running `fsdocs build --saveimages=all` flag, but it seems to have no effect. This is possibly due to #683. --- Looking through the markdown parser, it seems that this syntax should be supported to include an image: https://github.com/fsprojects/FSharp.Formatting/blob/2efb355823b8311f91a06566c0a3de86037a590d/src/FSharp.Formatting.Markdown/MarkdownParser.fs#L479-L498 And looking through the `BuildCommand`, it seems that remote and local images should be supported: https://github.com/fsprojects/FSharp.Formatting/blob/2efb355823b8311f91a06566c0a3de86037a590d/src/fsdocs-tool/BuildCommand.fs#L49-L71 Though, the `imageSaverOpt` value in `processFile` seems to only ever be passed into the `Literate` methods, which is what I assume the linked issue is in reference to.

🤖 *This is an automated response from Repo Assist.*

Coming back to this thread with a clearer breakdown of the current behaviour and the recommended workflow.

## How images in XML doc comments work today

When you use `--mdcomments` and write:

````fsharp
/// ![local image](images/pi.png)
let pi = 3.14159
```

The markdown is parsed and rendered as `(img src="images/pi.png" alt="local image" /)` in the generated HTML. The image path is used verbatim — `fsdocs` does **not** copy source-tree files referenced inside XML doc comments.

This is by design: `fsdocs` has no way to know where `images/pi.png` is relative to the source file, and it doesn't walk the source tree looking for assets.

## Recommended workflow

Put images in the `docs/` input directory, which is copied to the output automatically:

```
your-project/
├── docs/
│   └── content/
│       └── images/
│           └── pi.png   ← put images here
└── src/
    └── MyLib/
        └── MyModule.fs
````

Then reference them in XML doc comments using a root-relative path:

```fsharp
/// (img src="/content/images/pi.png" alt="Pi diagram" /)
let pi = 3.14159
```

Or in markdown comment mode (`--mdcomments`):

```fsharp
/// ![Pi diagram](/content/images/pi.png)
let pi = 3.14159
```

The leading `/` gives a site-root-relative URL that works regardless of how deep the API page is nested in the output.

> **Note:** The `\{\{fsdocs-root}}` template substitution is applied to the *template file*, not to the content of XML doc comments. So `\{\{fsdocs-root}}content/images/pi.png` in a doc comment will not be substituted — use an absolute site path like `/content/images/pi.png` instead.

## For `.fsx` literate scripts (different story)

If your content is in `.fsx` or `.md` files under `docs/`, images in `(** ![...](path) *)` blocks **are** resolved relative to the source file and copied to the output when using `--saveimages=all`. That's a separate pipeline from API docs.

## What a proper fix would look like

Automatically copying source-tree images referenced in XML doc comments would require:
1. Knowing the source file location for each XML doc entry (available, it's in the cracked project)
2. Resolving image paths relative to the source file
3. Copying images to `output/content/images/` and rewriting the `src` attribute

This is a medium-complexity enhancement — if there's maintainer appetite for it, happy to attempt an implementation.

pr.body:
🤖 *This PR was created by Repo Assist, an automated AI assistant.* Closes #927 ## Summary Adds support for one level of nested navigation categories using `/` as a separator in the `category` front-matter field: ```yaml --- category: Collections/Lists categoryindex: 1 index: 2 --- ``` This renders in the sidebar as: ``` Collections ← .nav-header (parent) Arrays ← .nav-sub-header - Pattern Matching Lists ← .nav-sub-header - Destructuring with Cons ``` **Design choices, matching the approach originally proposed on the issue:** - `/` was chosen as the separator to match Hugo/Docusaurus conventions. - Fully backwards compatible: a `category` with no `/` renders identically to today (verified by a dedicated regression test). - One nesting level (parent/sub) is supported; deeper nesting isn't handled. - Parent ordering uses the lowest `categoryindex` of any document under it, including documents in its sub-categories, so a parent doesn't need its own separate front-matter entry. - Documents that share a parent but have no sub-category are listed directly under the parent header, before any sub-headers. - When the site uses a custom `_menu_template.html` (no built-in sub-header support in the templating system), sub-categories are flattened into their parent's single group so existing templates keep working unmodified. ## Implementation - `src/fsdocs-tool/DocContent.fs`: `getNavigationEntriesFactory` now parses `category` into `(parent, subCategory option)`, groups/sorts at both levels, and renders `.nav-sub-header` list items in the non-templated (default theme) path. - `docs/content/fsdocs-default.css`: added `.nav-sub-header` styling (indented, smaller, same color family as `.nav-header`, with an `active` state). - `docs/content.fsx`: documented the new `category: Parent/Sub` syntax. - `RELEASE_NOTES.md`: added an `Unreleased` / `Added` entry. ## Test Status - ✅ `dotnet fantomas src tests docs --check` — clean, no formatting issues. - ✅ `dotnet build FSharp.Formatting.sln -c Release` — 0 errors, 0 warnings. - ✅ `dotnet test tests/fsdocs-tool.Tests` — 33/33 passed (added 2 new tests: one exercising the nested-category rendering end-to-end, one confirming a flat `category` renders unchanged). - ✅ `dotnet test tests/FSharp.Literate.Tests --filter FullyQualifiedName~DocContent` — 37/37 passed. - ✅ `dotnet test tests/FSharp.Literate.Tests` (full suite) — 146/146 passed. ## Background This reimplements the fix from #1105 (closed by ``@dsyme`` due to unrelated merge conflicts against a large Suave migration, not because the feature itself was rejected) against the current `DocContent.fs`/`getNavigationEntriesFactory` structure, since the file has since been substantially refactored. > Generated by 🌈 Repo Assist, see [workflow run](https://github.com/fsprojects/FSharp.Formatting/actions/runs/35408962900). comments.body:
/repo-assist

Thanks for picking this up. I'm going to close this PR. The sidebar code is neat, but it only covers the rendering, and that is the easy part. The parts I flagged as hard in #927 (next/previous links, menu templates, several levels) are either missing or worked around.

**Previous/next links can disagree with the sidebar.** The previous/next order still comes from sorting all pages by `(categoryindex, index)`, and category names play no part in it. The sidebar now uses its own order: pages without a sub-category come first, and each sub-group is placed by the lowest `categoryindex` in it. Two examples:

- `Collections/Arrays` and `Collections/Lists` share `categoryindex: 1`, which the docs in this PR suggest ("the parent's position is determined by the lowest `categoryindex` of any document under it"). The sidebar shows two groups, but next/previous mixes the Arrays and Lists pages by `index`. If two pages also share an `index`, the lookup finds the wrong page, and the second page gets the first page's links.
- A plain `Collections` page with `categoryindex: 3` is listed first in the sidebar. Next/previous puts it after a `Collections/Lists` page with `categoryindex: 2`.

**It is not backwards compatible.** Any existing category that contains a `/` changes meaning without warning: `CI/CD` becomes parent "CI" with sub-category "CD". You can't escape the `/`, and no message tells the user what happened.

**Custom menu templates get nothing.** With a `_menu_template.html`, the sub-categories are flattened into the parent group, and there is no new template parameter for a sub-header. Sites with their own template can't use the feature, and the sub-category names are lost.

**Only one level.** `A/B/C` gives parent `A` and sub-category `B/C`. The `(parent, sub option)` shape would have to be replaced by a real tree to go deeper, so this doesn't grow into multi-level support.

**The tests don't check much.** `shouldContainText "Lists"` also passes because of the page title. The "one parent header" claim is never checked, and every test page uses the same `categoryindex` and `index`, so ordering isn't really tested.

The original requester has moved on and the issue has no 👍 yet, so I don't want to commit to a front-matter syntax now. I'll keep #927 open to see if other people want this. If they do, I would start differently:

- Use a separate front-matter key (or an explicit tree) instead of overloading `category`, so existing category names keep working.
- Build the sidebar and the next/previous links from one ordered list of pages.
- Decide the menu template parameters before writing any rendering code.

content.title: Nesting Document Categories
content.body:
## Feature Request
I've been using this tool a lot more as of late, and I was curious if the discussion of nesting categories has ever come about.

Using the example structure below

```
Collections
| -- Overview
| -- Destructuring with Cons
| -- Pattern Matching Lists
| -- Pattern Matching Arrays
```

I think it would be nice to be able to create nested/subcategories like so.

```
Collections
| -- Overview
| -- Arrays
    | -- Pattern Matching
| -- Lists
    | -- Destructuring with Cons
    | -- Pattern Matching
```

My initial thoughts are we could potentially do this one of two ways (I'm sure there are better ideas as well).

1. Special Character Parsing
We could add some sort of character sequence which would be parsable for category so we know how to nest the folder appropriately.

``` markdown
---
category: Collections -> Lists
---
```

2. Additional Metadata
We could add an additional tag such as `parentCategory` which tells us how to nest the folder appropriately.

```markdown
---
category: Lists
parentCategory: Collections
---
```

### Notes

- If this is a desired feature, I would be willing to assist/work on this. 
- If this would come to pass, I can see people requesting the ability for the UI categories to be collapsible. I would imagine we'd want a way for the user to decide if they wanted the categories opened or closed on startup.

1. Parse `category` values containing `/` to extract `(parentCategory, childCategory)`.
2. In the nav rendering code (`BuildCommand.fs`, around line 770–792), group by parent first, then emit child categories as indented nav items within each parent group.
3. The existing `category-index` would control ordering within each parent.

The sidebar HTML structure would use nested `<ul>` elements with a `nav-sub-header` CSS class for child groups.

If you're willing to work on this, it would be a very welcome PR — and the nav rendering code is reasonably approachable. Happy to help outline the data model changes if useful!

**How to use it:**

Add a `/` separator to the `category` field in your front matter:

````yaml
---
category: Collections/Lists
categoryindex: 1
index: 2
---
```

This renders in the sidebar as:

```
Collections           ← parent header
  Arrays              ← sub-header
    - Pattern Matching
  Lists               ← sub-header
    - Destructuring with Cons
    - Pattern Matching
````

**Design choices:**
- The `/` separator was chosen to match Hugo/Docusaurus conventions and the approach suggested in `@1eyewonder`'s original proposal
- **Fully backwards compatible** — categories without `/` render identically to today
- One nesting level (parent/child) is supported; deeper nesting can be added later
- Parent category ordering is determined automatically by the minimum `categoryindex` of any child — no new front-matter key required
- When custom `_menu_template.html` files are used, the structure is flattened to the parent level so existing templates are unaffected

pr.title: [CI Fix] Fix gpui_apple build.rs: gpui::GPUI_MANIFEST_DIR was never resolvable
pr.body:
## What broke

Run #747 (`build-examples-macos` job, workflow run 35897738744) failed with:

```
error[E0433]: cannot find module or crate `gpui` in this scope
  --> crates/gpui-apple-gpui-unofficial/build.rs:103:9
103 |         gpui::GPUI_MANIFEST_DIR.into()
    |         ^^^^ use of unresolved module or unlinked crate `gpui`
```

## Root cause

The just-merged PR #301 patched `gpui_apple`'s `build.rs` (in `patch_gpui_apple_build_rs`, `xtask/src/transform.rs`) to replace a sibling-directory path lookup with `gpui::GPUI_MANIFEST_DIR.into()`, so registry installs (where `gpui_apple` and `gpui` live in separate versioned directories) can still find gpui's shader sources for `cbindgen`.

However, that patch was incomplete:

1. Build scripts can only see `[build-dependencies]`, not `[dependencies]`. `gpui_apple` never declared `gpui` as a build-dependency (the old approach was pure filesystem path math, no actual crate dependency), so `transform_dependencies` had nothing to transform there.
2. `GPUI_MANIFEST_DIR` was never defined anywhere — not in zed's upstream `gpui` crate, nor added by any transform patch.

So `gpui::GPUI_MANIFEST_DIR` could never resolve, in either local-path or published-registry builds. `cargo check` jobs stayed green because they don't compile `gpui_apple`'s build script in that configuration, but `cargo build --examples` does, which is why only `build-examples-macos` caught it.

## Fix

In `xtask/src/transform.rs`:

- Added `add_gpui_build_dependency`, which mirrors the already-transformed `[dependencies].gpui` entry (package alias + version/path) into `[build-dependencies].gpui` for the `gpui_apple` crate.
- Added `add_gpui_manifest_dir_const`, which inserts `pub const GPUI_MANIFEST_DIR: &str = env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR");` into gpui's own `src/lib.rs` during transform, so the constant the build.rs patch references actually exists.

Both are minimal, targeted additions to the transform tool — no generated files under `crates/` were touched directly.

## Testing

- `cargo build -p xtask` succeeds.
- `cargo test -p xtask` passes (27/27), including two new unit tests covering the build-dependency mirroring and the lib.rs const injection.

Documents changes from microsoft/aspire#20537

``@mitchdenny``

## Target branch

Targeting `release/13.6` — the latest release branch on `microsoft/aspire.dev` — because `release/14.0` (from the source PR milestone `14.0`) does not exist there.

## Why this is needed

microsoft/aspire#20537 simplified the terminal dock's empty state: it removed the resource-terminal-links subsection and the `TerminalDockPanelBody`/`TerminalDockResourceTerminals` strings, reducing the empty state to a heading, console icon, a plain-text "More information" link (no filled hover background), and the backtick-key hint. The PR body's own "User-facing usage" section states: "Open the empty terminal dock using the dashboard's terminal button or the backtick key. It shows **No docked terminals**, **More information**, and the hint to press backtick to hide the panel."

This specific empty-state experience (how to open it, what it shows, how to dismiss it) wasn't previously documented on aspire.dev.

Documents changes from microsoft/aspire#20527

``@JamesNK``

Targeting `release/13.6` — the latest release branch on `microsoft/aspire.dev` — because `release/14.0` (from the source PR milestone `14.0`) does not exist there.

## Why this PR is needed

microsoft/aspire#20527 updates Fluent UI Blazor Components/Icons to the 5.0.0 RTM release. Two of the resulting behavior changes are directly user-facing and match the PR's own "User-facing usage" section:

- The dashboard's navigation-rail overflow trigger now renders as a native button, with height, width, icon alignment, and hover styling matching the navigation toggle and other rail items in light and dark themes.
- Page-state updates now persist session state before navigating; if the Blazor circuit already disconnected, the expected `JSDisconnectedException` is caught and navigation is skipped instead of surfacing an unhandled error.

These are exactly the kind of dashboard UI/behavior changes documented in the "What's new" release notes' "More telemetry and independent dashboard sessions" list.

## What changed

- `src/frontend/src/content/docs/whats-new/aspire-13-6.mdx`: added two bullet points to the existing dashboard improvements list documenting the AppBar overflow button styling fix and the disconnected-circuit navigation fix.

No new pages were created; this updates an existing "What's new" page.

pr.title: [docs] Remove terminal commands feature flag references
pr.body:
Documents changes from microsoft/aspire#20525

``@mitchdenny``

## Target branch

Targeting `release/13.6` — the latest release branch on `microsoft/aspire.dev` — because the source PR milestone `14.0` (mapped to `release/14.0`) does not exist there yet.

## Why this is needed

microsoft/aspire#20525 removes the `features.terminalCommandsEnabled` feature flag, making `aspire terminal`, `aspire terminal ps`, and `aspire terminal attach` available without any opt-in configuration step. The docs previously instructed readers to run `aspire config set features.terminalCommandsEnabled true` before using these commands, which is now inaccurate.

## What changed

- `reference/cli/commands/aspire-terminal.mdx`: removed the "hidden behind a feature flag" paragraph and the `aspire config set features.terminalCommandsEnabled true` snippet.
- `reference/cli/commands/aspire-terminal-ps.mdx`: removed the feature-flag sentence; kept the `terminals.v1` capability requirement.
- `reference/cli/commands/aspire-terminal-attach.mdx`: removed the feature-flag sentence.
- `app-host/with-terminal.mdx`: updated the "Work with terminals from the CLI" section to state the commands work without a configuration step, removing the enable snippet.

Sidebar `Preview` badges and the `terminals.v1` AppHost-capability requirement were left as-is, since those are unrelated to this flag removal. Historical `whats-new/aspire-13-5.mdx` and `aspire-13-6.mdx` release notes were intentionally left unchanged since they document past releases as they shipped.

## Files modified

- `src/frontend/src/content/docs/reference/cli/commands/aspire-terminal.mdx`
- `src/frontend/src/content/docs/reference/cli/commands/aspire-terminal-ps.mdx`
- `src/frontend/src/content/docs/reference/cli/commands/aspire-terminal-attach.mdx`
- `src/frontend/src/content/docs/app-host/with-terminal.mdx`

No new pages were created; all four existing pages were updated in place.

pr.title: [docs] Unify experimental polyglot AppHost feature keys
pr.body:
Documents changes from microsoft/aspire#20481

``@sebastienros``

## Target branch

Targeting `release/13.6` — the latest release branch on `microsoft/aspire.dev` — because the source PR has no milestone or `release/*` base ref to derive a more specific target.

## Why this is needed

microsoft/aspire#20481 renamed the experimental polyglot AppHost feature flags from `experimentalPolyglot:<language>` (colon-separated) to flat `experimentalPolyglot<Language>` names, because `aspire config set` interpreted the colon as a configuration-object separator and wrote an invalid nested `features` object. This is a breaking change (label `breaking-change`) with an explicit "User-facing usage" section in the source PR showing the new flag names (`experimentalPolyglotJava`, `experimentalPolyglotGo`, `experimentalPolyglotPython`, `experimentalPolyglotRust`), so the docs site's existing references to the old colon-based key needed updating.

## What changed

- `src/frontend/src/content/docs/integrations/frameworks/go/go-host.mdx`: updated the example command from `aspire config set features:experimentalPolyglot:go true --global` to `aspire config set features.experimentalPolyglotGo true --global`.
- `src/frontend/src/content/docs/reference/cli/configuration.mdx`: updated the same example command, and removed a now-inaccurate note that some feature flags use a `:<language>` suffix (no flag uses that format anymore).
- `src/frontend/src/content/docs/reference/cli/includes/config-settings-table.md`: renamed all four `features.experimentalPolyglot:<lang>` table rows to the new flat `features.experimentalPolyglot<Lang>` key names (Go, Java, Python, Rust).

No new pages were created; all three existing pages were updated in place to reflect the renamed keys.

content.title: CLI configuration reference: use the flat experimentalPolyglot keys
content.body:
Part of microsoft/aspire#21115

The CLI configuration reference on `release/17.0` documents the four language feature flags with a colon in the key, for example `features.experimentalPolyglot:go`. microsoft/aspire#20481 (merged to `main`) renamed them to `experimentalPolyglotGo`, `experimentalPolyglotJava`, `experimentalPolyglotPython` and `experimentalPolyglotRust`, and its description says the old colon keys no longer enable the languages. The `release/17.0` branch of microsoft/aspire still reads the colon names (`src/Aspire.Cli/KnownFeatures.cs` L32-35 at 55867ce9d3) and the open sync PR microsoft/aspire#20570 carries the flat names (same lines at a0372fd67a), so these docs are accurate today and become wrong when that sync lands. Target branch is `release/17.0`; line numbers are microsoft/aspire.dev `release/17.0` at 5c48cfbd9c. microsoft/aspire.dev `main` (fa51b996d9) was also checked: the six pages cited below and `src/frontend/src/data/schemas/` are identical there, so the line numbers hold on both branches.

Related: microsoft/aspire#20481 (Unify experimental polyglot AppHost feature keys), microsoft/aspire#20570 (Sync Aspire 17 release branch with main and release metadata), microsoft/aspire.dev#1771 (closed: [docs] Unify experimental polyglot AppHost feature keys), microsoft/aspire.dev#1809 (open draft: [docs] Document container tunnel base image configuration), microsoft/aspire.dev#1814 (Sync Aspire CLI config schemas through 13.6.0 and fix config docs), microsoft/aspire.dev#1924 (Document the Go AppHost: getting started, conventions and CLI references), microsoft/aspire#21106 ([Go AppHost GA] Remove the feature flag and expose Go templates), microsoft/aspire.dev#700 (Document Go language support for polyglot AppHosts).

### Checklist

- [ ] Rename the four rows in the settings table. `src/frontend/src/content/docs/reference/cli/includes/config-settings-table.md` L14-17 list `features.experimentalPolyglot:go`, `:java`, `:python` and `:rust` (default `false`). The table is included by three pages (`reference/cli/commands/aspire-config.mdx:55`, `reference/cli/commands/aspire-config-set.mdx:62` and `reference/cli/configuration.mdx:110`), so one edit fixes all of them. Fix: rename the rows to `features.experimentalPolyglotGo`, `features.experimentalPolyglotJava`, `features.experimentalPolyglotPython` and `features.experimentalPolyglotRust`, and drop the Go row instead if microsoft/aspire#21183 (open draft; removes the Go flag, tracked by microsoft/aspire#21106) lands first.
- [ ] Remove the colon workaround from the caution block. `config-settings-table.md` L32-37 is a `:::caution` saying `aspire config set` cannot write keys that contain `.` or `:`. Its first bullet (L35) says that without `--global` the CLI writes a nested `experimentalPolyglot` object that later commands cannot load, and tells readers to use `--global` or to edit the file by hand. microsoft/aspire#20481 was written to fix exactly that problem (its description says the flat names make `aspire config set` write a loadable file), so the bullet is wrong for a CLI that has the flat names. The package-ID bullet (L36) is a separate limitation and stays. Fix: delete the L35 bullet.
- [ ] Fix the feature-flag steps on the configuration page. `src/frontend/src/content/docs/reference/cli/configuration.mdx` L177-178 say that some language flags "use a `:<language>` suffix", L184-188 show `aspire config set features.experimentalPolyglot:go true --global` under the title "Enable global Go support", and L190-192 say "Always set `experimentalPolyglot:<language>` flags with `--global`, or add them to the local `aspire.config.json` file by hand". All three describe the colon spelling. Fix: drop the suffix sentence and the always-global paragraph, and change the example to a flag that survives microsoft/aspire#21183 (or to `features.experimentalPolyglotGo` if that PR does not land).
- [ ] Update the Rust get-started note. `src/frontend/src/content/docs/integrations/frameworks/rust/rust-get-started.mdx` L47 says a Rust AppHost is turned on with "the `features.experimentalPolyglot:rust` configuration setting". Fix: use `features.experimentalPolyglotRust`.
- [ ] Check the Go page after microsoft/aspire.dev#1924 lands. `src/frontend/src/content/docs/integrations/frameworks/go/go-host.mdx` L518 shows a third spelling, `aspire config set features:experimentalPolyglot:go true --global` (a colon after `features`), in the "Experimental Go AppHost templates" section (L513-532). microsoft/aspire.dev#1924 rewrites that page (its head c4a58eb10c has no `experimentalPolyglot` in it) and its new `go-apphost.mdx` already uses the flat spelling (L11, L14 and L17), so after microsoft/aspire.dev#1924 merges the site shows both spellings until this issue is done. Fix: re-run `git grep experimentalPolyglot` when microsoft/aspire.dev#1924 merges and rename anything left.
- [ ] Use the flat names in the AppHost-language registry if that stack is revived. The open draft microsoft/aspire.dev#1634 (and the PRs stacked on it) adds `src/frontend/src/data/apphost-languages.json`, whose `featureFlag` values use the colon spelling (`experimentalPolyglot:go` and the other three; L42, L56, L70 and L84 at 69e3c6b14c, and the same at the head of microsoft/aspire.dev#1638, 83dda4c480). Where those values are shown to readers is unverified. Fix: use the flat names there before the registry ships.
- [ ] Leave the per-release schema snapshots alone. Each of the 24 files `src/frontend/src/data/schemas/aspire-config.13.2.0.schema.json` through `aspire-config.13.6.0.schema.json` has four lines that mention `experimentalPolyglot`. Per the description of microsoft/aspire.dev#1814 (not run), they are generated from each released CLI and never rewritten after release, so a repo-wide search will list them but they should not be edited, and a 17.x snapshot should carry the flat names without a manual edit. Fix: exclude `src/frontend/src/data/schemas/` from the final search.

### Recommended order

Land the docs change together with, or just after, the microsoft/aspire#20570 sync, never before it, because until then the `release/17.0` CLI still reads the colon names. Do it in one pull request: the settings table and its caution, the configuration page and the Rust note first; the Go page and the registry values depend on what microsoft/aspire.dev#1924 and the registry stack have done by then. Finish with a repo-wide search. The open draft microsoft/aspire.dev#1809 (conflicting with `release/17.0`) also edits `config-settings-table.md` and `reference/cli/configuration.mdx` without touching the `experimentalPolyglot` text, so whichever pull request lands second re-checks the line numbers above.

### Done when

`git grep experimentalPolyglot` on the branch finds only the historical schema snapshots and the flat names; every page uses the names the `release/17.0` CLI reads; no page presents `--global` as a workaround for the old colon keys; and the Go flag row and examples match whatever microsoft/aspire#21183 decides.

pr.title: [docs] Document MongoDB EF Core net10.0 support and dependency consolidation
pr.body:
Documents changes from microsoft/aspire#20607

``@eerhardt``

## Target branch

Targeting `release/13.6` — the latest release branch on `microsoft/aspire.dev` — because `release/17.0` (from the source PR milestone `17.0`) does not exist there.

## Why this is needed

microsoft/aspire#20607 consolidated MongoDB dependency versions (`MongoDB.Driver` to 3.12.0 across all target frameworks, `MongoDB.EntityFrameworkCore` to 8.4.4/9.1.4/10.0.4 for net8.0/net9.0/net10.0 respectively) and added a new `net10.0` target framework asset for `Aspire.MongoDB.EntityFrameworkCore`, which previously only shipped `net8.0` and `net9.0` because the provider didn't support EF Core 10. This is a user-facing change to the package's supported target framework matrix, and no existing docs page named the new `net10.0` support or the consolidated dependency versions, so a docs update was required (triggered signal: `target_framework_changed`, evidence: `Aspire.MongoDB.EntityFrameworkCore.csproj` TargetFrameworks changed from `$(DefaultTargetFramework);net9.0` to `$(AllTargetFrameworks)`).

- **`src/frontend/src/content/docs/integrations/databases/efcore/mongodb/mongodb-efcore-get-started.mdx`**: Updated the client-integration bullet to state the package targets `net8.0`, `net9.0`, and `net10.0`.

pr.title: [docs] Document dashboard connection lost message for otel logs/spans --follow
pr.body:
Documents changes from microsoft/aspire#20542

``@JamesNK``

**Target branch**: Targeting `release/17.0` based on the source PR milestone `17.0`.

## Why

microsoft/aspire#20542 reduces AppHost log noise and adds a new user-visible behavior: when `aspire otel logs --follow` or `aspire otel spans --follow` is streaming and the dashboard connection closes (an expected disconnect, such as dashboard shutdown or a truncated chunked response), the CLI now prints "The connection to the dashboard was lost." to stderr and exits successfully, instead of surfacing a raw I/O exception. This is implemented by `StreamReader.ReadLinesWithDisconnectHandlingAsync` and the new `TelemetryCommandStrings.DashboardConnectionLost` resource string, and is covered by `TelemetryFollowTests`.

The other changes in the source PR (auxiliary backchannel disconnect handling in `aspire ps`, resource-readiness log suppression, HTTP client factory log filtering) only reduce internal Debug-level log noise on paths that were never documented, so no further doc updates were needed for those.

## What changed

- `src/frontend/src/content/docs/reference/cli/commands/aspire-otel-logs.mdx`: Updated the `-f, --follow` option description to note the new dashboard-disconnect message and successful exit behavior.
- `src/frontend/src/content/docs/reference/cli/commands/aspire-otel-spans.mdx`: Same update for the `aspire otel spans` command.

Both are updates to existing pages; no new pages were created.

The GitHub Policy Service is created and maintained by the GitHub Inside Microsoft team at Microsoft 1ES. This service is the foundation for the compliance and governance efforts on our GitHub instances. In a nutshell, the Policy Service manages GitHub organizations and repositories using Config-As-Code.

This instance is dedicated to the .NET Foundation and its projects.

Microsoft project maintainers who are employees can learn more about this app, including support and feedback opportunities, at [GitOps](https://aka.ms/1es-gitops).
For commands to interact with the bots you have to use @dotnet-policy-service.

pr.title: [docs] docs: regenerate API diffs and release notes
pr.body:
## Description

Regenerates prepared API-diff facts and release-note pages, including reviewed consumer-facing prose for 4.152.1, 4.154.0, and the next unreleased line.

**Related issues**

None.

**Required skia PR**

None.

**Areas affected**

- [ ] Managed API (`binding/`)
- [ ] Native / C API (`externals/skia/src/c`, `include/c`)
- [ ] Generated P/Invoke bindings
- [ ] Native dependency or Skia update (libpng, HarfBuzz, FreeType, zlib, milestone bump, ...)
- [ ] Views & integrations (MAUI, Uno, WPF, WinUI, Blazor, ...)
- [ ] Rendering output / visual behavior
- [ ] Performance
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] Build, packaging, or CI
- [x] Documentation or samples

## Changes

None — documentation and generated API-diff/release-note artifacts only; no managed or native API behavior changes.

## Testing

Rendered the complete release-note set with `python3 scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-render.py --all`.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated (if omitted, explain why above)
- [x] `Changes` above lists all public API and behavioral changes (or "None.")
- [x] New/changed public API? Filed a docs issue in [mono/SkiaSharp-API-docs](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp-API-docs/issues) so reference docs can be written later
- [x] Native change? Companion `mono/skia` PR linked above and bindings regenerated

app.name: Dotnet Policy Service
app.description:
The GitHub Policy Service is created and maintained by the GitHub Inside Microsoft team at Microsoft 1ES. This service is the foundation for the compliance and governance efforts on our GitHub instances. In a nutshell, the Policy Service manages GitHub organizations and repositories using Config-As-Code.

This instance is dedicated to the .NET Foundation and its projects.

Microsoft project maintainers who are employees can learn more about this app, including support and feedback opportunities, at [GitOps](https://aka.ms/1es-gitops).
For commands to interact with the bots you have to use @dotnet-policy-service.

pr.title: [docs] docs: regenerate API diffs and release notes
pr.body:
## Description

Regenerates the API diff facts and release-notes pages from the prepared release data. Adds curated consumer-facing prose for the affected release lines and rebuilds the release index and TOC.

**Related issues**

None.

**Required skia PR**

None.

**Areas affected**

- [ ] Managed API (`binding/`)
- [ ] Native / C API (`externals/skia/src/c`, `include/c`)
- [ ] Generated P/Invoke bindings
- [ ] Native dependency or Skia update (libpng, HarfBuzz, FreeType, zlib, milestone bump, ...)
- [ ] Views & integrations (MAUI, Uno, WPF, WinUI, Blazor, ...)
- [ ] Rendering output / visual behavior
- [ ] Performance
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] Build, packaging, or CI
- [x] Documentation or samples

## Changes

None - documentation and generated release-note/API-diff artifacts only; no public API or runtime behavior changes.

## Testing

Validated all release-note prose and rendered every release page, the release index, and TOC with `python3 scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-render.py --all`.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated (if omitted, explain why above)
- [x] `Changes` above lists all public API and behavioral changes (or "None.")
- [ ] New/changed public API? Added or updated accurate source `///` documentation and regenerated bindings when applicable
- [ ] Native change? Companion `mono/skia` PR linked above and bindings regenerated

### Continuously build, test, and deploy to any platform and cloud

[Azure Pipelines](https://azure.microsoft.com/services/devops/pipelines/) offers cloud-hosted pipelines for Linux, macOS, and Windows with 10 free parallel jobs and unlimited minutes for open source projects.

:v: **Any language, platform, and cloud**
Build, test, and deploy Node.js, Python,  Java, PHP, Ruby, Go, C/C++, C#, Android, and iOS apps. Run in parallel on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Deploy to cloud providers like Azure, AWS, and GCP. Distribute mobile apps through beta channels and app stores.

:whale2: **Native container support**
Create new containers with ease and push them to any registry. Deploy containers to independent hosts or Kubernetes.

:muscle: **Advanced workflows and features**
Easy build chaining and multi-phased builds. Support for YAML, test integration, release gates, reporting, and more.

:wrench: **Extensible**
Use a range of build, test, and deployment tasks built by the community – hundreds of extensions from Slack to SonarCloud. You can even deploy from other CI systems, like Jenkins. Webhooks and REST APIs help you integrate.

:blue_heart: **Free, to you from Azure Pipelines**
Free cloud-hosted builds for public and private repositories.

...

Microsoft project maintainers who are employees can learn more about this app, including support and feedback opportunities, at [GitOps](https://aka.ms/1es-gitops).

## Description

Regenerates the release-note facts and API-diff outputs, adds reviewed consumer-facing prose for the affected historical and current release pages, and rebuilds the release index and TOC.

**Related issues**

None.

**Required skia PR**

None.

**Areas affected**

- [ ] Managed API (`binding/`)
- [ ] Native / C API (`externals/skia/src/c`, `include/c`)
- [ ] Generated P/Invoke bindings
- [ ] Native dependency or Skia update (libpng, HarfBuzz, FreeType, zlib, milestone bump, ...)
- [ ] Views & integrations (MAUI, Uno, WPF, WinUI, Blazor, ...)
- [ ] Rendering output / visual behavior
- [ ] Performance
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] Build, packaging, or CI
- [x] Documentation or samples

## Changes

None — documentation and generated API-diff/release-note output only; no public API or runtime behavior changed.

## Testing

Rendered the full release-note set with `python3 scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-render.py --all`.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated (not applicable: documentation-only change)
- [x] `Changes` above lists all public API and behavioral changes (or "None.")
- [ ] New/changed public API? Added or updated accurate source `///` documentation and regenerated bindings when applicable
- [ ] Native change? Companion `mono/skia` PR linked above and bindings regenerated

Regenerates API diffs and release-notes facts, refreshes consumer-facing prose for the affected release pages, and renders the release index.

None.

- [ ] Rendering output / visual behavior
- [ ] Performance
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] Build, packaging, or CI
- [x] Documentation or samples

None - documentation and generated API-diff metadata only; no public API or runtime behavior changes.

Ran `python3 scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-render.py --all`.

- [x] `Changes` above lists all public API and behavioral changes (or "None.")
- [ ] New/changed public API? Added or updated accurate source `///` documentation and regenerated bindings when applicable
- [ ] Native change? Companion `mono/skia` PR linked above and bindings regenerated

The GitHub Policy Service is created and maintained by the GitHub Inside Microsoft team at Microsoft 1ES. This service is the foundation for the compliance and governance efforts on our GitHub instances. This instance is dedicated to the .NET Foundation and its projects.

Microsoft project maintainers who are employees can learn more about this app, including support and feedback opportunities, at [GitOps](https://aka.ms/1es-gitops).
For commands to interact with the bots you have to use @dotnet-policy-service.

[Azure Pipelines](https://azure.microsoft.com/services/devops/pipelines/) offers cloud-hosted pipelines for Linux, macOS, and Windows with 10 free parallel jobs and unlimited minutes for open source projects.

:whale2: **Native container support**
Create new containers with ease and push them to any registry. Deploy containers to independent hosts or Kubernetes.

Easy build chaining and multi-phased builds. Support for YAML, test integration, release gates, reporting, and more.

:wrench: **Extensible**
Use a range of build, test, and deployment tasks built by the community – hundreds of extensions from Slack to SonarCloud. You can even deploy from other CI systems, like Jenkins. Webhooks and REST APIs help you integrate.

:blue_heart: **Free, to you from Azure Pipelines**
Free cloud-hosted builds for public and private repositories.

[Azure Pipelines](https://azure.microsoft.com/services/devops/pipelines/) offers cloud-hosted pipelines for Linux, macOS, and Windows with 10 free parallel jobs and unlimited minutes for open source projects.

:v: **Any language, platform, and cloud**
Build, test, and deploy Node.js, Python,  Java, PHP, Ruby, Go, C/C++, C#, Android, and iOS apps. Run in parallel on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Deploy to cloud providers like Azure, AWS, and GCP. Distribute mobile apps through beta channels and app stores.

:whale2: **Native container support**
Create new containers with ease and push them to any registry. Deploy containers to independent hosts or Kubernetes.

:muscle: **Advanced workflows and features**
Easy build chaining and multi-phased builds. Support for YAML, test integration, release gates, reporting, and more.

:wrench: **Extensible**
Use a range of build, test, and deployment tasks built by the community – hundreds of extensions from Slack to SonarCloud. You can even deploy from other CI systems, like Jenkins. Webhooks and REST APIs help you integrate.

:blue_heart: **Free, to you from Azure Pipelines**
Free cloud-hosted builds for public and private repositories.

pr.title: [docs] docs: regenerate API diffs and release notes
pr.body:
## Description

Regenerates the deterministic API-diff facts and release-note pages, then adds reviewed consumer-facing prose for the updated unreleased 4.150.4, 4.151.4, 4.152.2, 4.153.0, and 4.154.0 lines. This keeps the documentation site and package-facing API documentation release notes synchronized with the prepared release metadata.

**Related issues**

None.

**Required skia PR**

None.

**Areas affected**

- [ ] Managed API (`binding/`)
- [ ] Native / C API (`externals/skia/src/c`, `include/c`)
- [ ] Generated P/Invoke bindings
- [ ] Native dependency or Skia update (libpng, HarfBuzz, FreeType, zlib, milestone bump, ...)
- [ ] Views & integrations (MAUI, Uno, WPF, WinUI, Blazor, ...)
- [ ] Rendering output / visual behavior
- [ ] Performance
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] Build, packaging, or CI
- [x] Documentation or samples

## Changes

None — documentation and generated API-diff/release-note metadata only; no public API or runtime behavior changes.

## Testing

Ran `python3 scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-render.py --all`, which rendered all 84 release-note pages and regenerated the release TOC and index successfully.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated (not applicable: documentation-only generated output)
- [x] `Changes` above lists all public API and behavioral changes (or "None.")
- [x] New/changed public API? Added or updated accurate source `///` documentation and regenerated bindings when applicable (not applicable)
- [x] Native change? Companion `mono/skia` PR linked above and bindings regenerated (not applicable)

:whale2: **Native container support**
Create new containers with ease and push them to any registry. Deploy containers to independent hosts or Kubernetes.

:wrench: **Extensible**
Use a range of build, test, and deployment tasks built by the community – hundreds of extensions from Slack to SonarCloud. You can even deploy from other CI systems, like Jenkins. Webhooks and REST APIs help you integrate.

:blue_heart: **Free, to you from Azure Pipelines**
Free cloud-hosted builds for public and private repositories.

[Azure Pipelines](https://azure.microsoft.com/services/devops/pipelines/) offers cloud-hosted pipelines for Linux, macOS, and Windows with 10 free parallel jobs and unlimited minutes for open source projects.

:v: **Any language, platform, and cloud**
Build, test, and deploy Node.js, Python,  Java, PHP, Ruby, Go, C/C++, C#, Android, and iOS apps. Run in parallel on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Deploy to cloud providers like Azure, AWS, and GCP. Distribute mobile apps through beta channels and app stores.

:whale2: **Native container support**
Create new containers with ease and push them to any registry. Deploy containers to independent hosts or Kubernetes.

:muscle: **Advanced workflows and features**
Easy build chaining and multi-phased builds. Support for YAML, test integration, release gates, reporting, and more.

:wrench: **Extensible**
Use a range of build, test, and deployment tasks built by the community – hundreds of extensions from Slack to SonarCloud. You can even deploy from other CI systems, like Jenkins. Webhooks and REST APIs help you integrate.

:blue_heart: **Free, to you from Azure Pipelines**
Free cloud-hosted builds for public and private repositories.

[Azure Pipelines](https://azure.microsoft.com/services/devops/pipelines/) offers cloud-hosted pipelines for Linux, macOS, and Windows with 10 free parallel jobs and unlimited minutes for open source projects.

:v: **Any language, platform, and cloud**
Build, test, and deploy Node.js, Python,  Java, PHP, Ruby, Go, C/C++, C#, Android, and iOS apps. Run in parallel on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Deploy to cloud providers like Azure, AWS, and GCP. Distribute mobile apps through beta channels and app stores.

:whale2: **Native container support**
Create new containers with ease and push them to any registry. Deploy containers to independent hosts or Kubernetes.

:muscle: **Advanced workflows and features**
Easy build chaining and multi-phased builds. Support for YAML, test integration, release gates, reporting, and more.

:wrench: **Extensible**
Use a range of build, test, and deployment tasks built by the community – hundreds of extensions from Slack to SonarCloud. You can even deploy from other CI systems, like Jenkins. Webhooks and REST APIs help you integrate.

:blue_heart: **Free, to you from Azure Pipelines**
Free cloud-hosted builds for public and private repositories.

### Continuously build, test, and deploy to any platform and cloud

[Azure Pipelines](https://azure.microsoft.com/services/devops/pipelines/) offers cloud-hosted pipelines for Linux, macOS, and Windows with 10 free parallel jobs and unlimited minutes for open source projects.

:v: **Any language, platform, and cloud**
Build, test, and deploy Node.js, Python,  Java, PHP, Ruby, Go, C/C++, C#, Android, and iOS apps. Run in parallel on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Deploy to cloud providers like Azure, AWS, and GCP. Distribute mobile apps through beta channels and app stores.

:whale2: **Native container support**
Create new containers with ease and push them to any registry. Deploy containers to independent hosts or Kubernetes.

:muscle: **Advanced workflows and features**
Easy build chaining and multi-phased builds. Support for YAML, test integration, release gates, reporting, and more.

:wrench: **Extensible**
Use a range of build, test, and deployment tasks built by the community – hundreds of extensions from Slack to SonarCloud. You can even deploy from other CI systems, like Jenkins. Webhooks and REST APIs help you integrate.

:blue_heart: **Free, to you from Azure Pipelines**
Free cloud-hosted builds for public and private repositories.

...

app.name: Dotnet Policy Service
app.description:
The GitHub Policy Service is created and maintained by the GitHub Inside Microsoft team at Microsoft 1ES. This service is the foundation for the compliance and governance efforts on our GitHub instances. In a nutshell, the Policy Service manages GitHub organizations and repositories using Config-As-Code.

This instance is dedicated to the .NET Foundation and its projects.

Microsoft project maintainers who are employees can learn more about this app, including support and feedback opportunities, at [GitOps](https://aka.ms/1es-gitops).
For commands to interact with the bots you have to use @dotnet-policy-service.

repository.name: SkiaSharp
repository.description: SkiaSharp is a cross-platform 2D graphics API for .NET platforms based on Google's Skia Graphics Library. It provides a comprehensive 2D API that can be used across mobile, server and desktop models to render images.

pr.title: [docs] docs: regenerate API diffs and release notes
pr.body:
## Description

Regenerates the API-diff documentation and release-notes facts restored from the Prepare phase, adds reviewed prose for the affected release lines, and renders the release pages and aggregates.

**Related issues**

None.

**Required skia PR**

None.

**Areas affected**

- [ ] Managed API (`binding/`)
- [ ] Native / C API (`externals/skia/src/c`, `include/c`)
- [ ] Generated P/Invoke bindings
- [ ] Native dependency or Skia update (libpng, HarfBuzz, FreeType, zlib, milestone bump, ...)
- [ ] Views & integrations (MAUI, Uno, WPF, WinUI, Blazor, ...)
- [ ] Rendering output / visual behavior
- [ ] Performance
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] Build, packaging, or CI
- [x] Documentation or samples

## Changes

None — documentation and generated API-diff/release-note artifacts only.

## Testing

Ran `python3 scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-render.py` for every page listed in `output/files-to-polish.txt`, followed by `python3 scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-render.py --all`. All 84 release pages, `TOC.yml`, and `index.md` rendered successfully.

## Checklist

- [ ] Tests added or updated (not applicable: documentation generation only)
- [x] `Changes` above lists all public API and behavioral changes (or "None.")
- [ ] New/changed public API? Added or updated accurate source `///` documentation and regenerated bindings when applicable (not applicable)
- [ ] Native change? Companion `mono/skia` PR linked above and bindings regenerated (not applicable)

[Azure Pipelines](https://azure.microsoft.com/services/devops/pipelines/) offers cloud-hosted pipelines for Linux, macOS, and Windows with 10 free parallel jobs and unlimited minutes for open source projects.

:wrench: **Extensible**
Use a range of build, test, and deployment tasks built by the community – hundreds of extensions from Slack to SonarCloud. You can even deploy from other CI systems, like Jenkins. Webhooks and REST APIs help you integrate.

:blue_heart: **Free, to you from Azure Pipelines**

app.name: Dotnet Policy Service
app.description:
The GitHub Policy Service is created and maintained by the GitHub Inside Microsoft team at Microsoft 1ES. This service is the foundation for the compliance and governance efforts on our GitHub instances. In a nutshell, the Policy Service manages GitHub organizations and repositories using Config-As-Code.

This instance is dedicated to the .NET Foundation and its projects.

Microsoft project maintainers who are employees can learn more about this app, including support and feedback opportunities, at [GitOps](https://aka.ms/1es-gitops).
For commands to interact with the bots you have to use @dotnet-policy-service.

pr.title: [docs] docs: regenerate API diffs and release notes
pr.body:
## Description

Regenerates the API-diff documentation and release-notes source facts, adds reviewed consumer-facing prose for the prepared release pages, and renders the release pages, TOC, and index from those inputs.

**Related issues**

None.

**Required skia PR**

None.

**Areas affected**

- [x] Documentation or samples

## Changes

None — documentation generation and release-note prose only; no public API or behavioral changes.

## Testing

Ran `python3 scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-render.py --all` successfully. The renderer regenerated 87 pages and the release-notes TOC/index; `git diff --check` passed.

## Checklist

- [ ] Tests added or updated (not applicable: documentation-only change)
