## Description

Regenerates the release-note facts and API-diff documentation, adds curated consumer-facing prose for the affected release lines, and renders every release page plus the release index and TOC.

**Related issues**

None.

**Required skia PR**

None.

**Areas affected**

- [ ] Managed API (`binding/`)
- [ ] Native / C API (`externals/skia/src/c`, `include/c`)
- [ ] Generated P/Invoke bindings
- [ ] Native dependency or Skia update (libpng, HarfBuzz, FreeType, zlib, milestone bump, ...)
- [ ] Views & integrations (MAUI, Uno, WPF, WinUI, Blazor, ...)
- [ ] Rendering output / visual behavior
- [ ] Performance
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] Build, packaging, or CI
- [x] Documentation or samples

## Changes

Updates generated API-diff and release-note documentation only; no public API or runtime behavior changes are introduced by this PR.

## Testing

Ran `python3 scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-render.py --all`, which rendered all 88 pages and regenerated the release TOC and index.

## Checklist

- [ ] Tests added or updated (not applicable: documentation-only generated release-note update)
- [x] `Changes` above lists all public API and behavioral changes (or "None.")
- [ ] New/changed public API? Added or updated accurate source `///` documentation and regenerated bindings when applicable

pr.title: [docs] docs: regenerate API diffs and release notes
pr.body:
## Description

Regenerates release-note facts, API diffs, and rendered release pages for the 4.150 through 4.155 lines. Adds reviewed consumer-facing prose for every page identified by the Prepare phase and rebuilds the release index and TOC from the committed source JSON.

**Related issues**

None.

**Required skia PR**

None.

**Areas affected**

- [x] Documentation or samples
- [ ] Managed API (`binding/`)
- [ ] Native / C API (`externals/skia/src/c`, `include/c`)
- [ ] Generated P/Invoke bindings
- [ ] Native dependency or Skia update (libpng, HarfBuzz, FreeType, zlib, milestone bump, ...)
- [ ] Views & integrations (MAUI, Uno, WPF, WinUI, Blazor, ...)
- [ ] Rendering output / visual behavior
- [ ] Performance
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] Build, packaging, or CI

## Changes

None — documentation and generated API-diff/release-note artifacts only; no public API or runtime behavior changed.

## Testing

Ran `python3 scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-render.py --all`, which successfully rendered all 89 release-note pages and regenerated the shared TOC and index.

## Checklist

- [ ] Tests added or updated (documentation-only change)
- [x] `Changes` above lists all public API and behavioral changes (or "None.")
- [ ] New/changed public API? Added or updated accurate source `///` documentation and regenerated bindings when applicable
- [ ] Native change? Companion `mono/skia` PR linked above and bindings regenerated

pr.body:
## Description

Regenerates the API-diff tree and release documentation from the prepared data, adding reviewed consumer-facing prose for the 4.150 through 4.155 release pages. The renderer also rebuilds the release index and TOC.

**Related issues**

None.

**Required skia PR**

None.

**Areas affected**

- [ ] Managed API (`binding/`)
- [ ] Native / C API (`externals/skia/src/c`, `include/c`)
- [ ] Generated P/Invoke bindings
- [ ] Native dependency or Skia update (libpng, HarfBuzz, FreeType, zlib, milestone bump, ...)
- [ ] Views & integrations (MAUI, Uno, WPF, WinUI, Blazor, ...)
- [ ] Rendering output / visual behavior
- [ ] Performance
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] Build, packaging, or CI
- [x] Documentation or samples

## Changes

None — documentation regeneration only; no public API or runtime behavior changes.

## Testing

Ran `python3 scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-render.py --all` successfully, which validated all prose inputs and regenerated 89 release pages plus the TOC and index.

## Checklist

- [ ] Tests added or updated (not applicable: documentation-only regeneration)
- [x] `Changes` above lists all public API and behavioral changes (or "None.")
- [ ] New/changed public API? Added or updated accurate source `///` documentation and regenerated bindings when applicable (not applicable)
- [ ] Native change? Companion `mono/skia` PR linked above and bindings regenerated (not applicable)

pr.title: [docs] docs: regenerate API diffs and release notes
pr.body:
## Description

Regenerates the deterministic API diffs and release-note facts, adds reviewed consumer-facing prose for the affected release lines, and renders the website pages, TOC, and index from those sources.

**Related issues**

None.

**Required skia PR**

None.

**Areas affected**

- [ ] Managed API (`binding/`)
- [ ] Native / C API (`externals/skia/src/c`, `include/c`)
- [ ] Generated P/Invoke bindings
- [ ] Native dependency or Skia update (libpng, HarfBuzz, FreeType, zlib, milestone bump, ...)
- [ ] Views & integrations (MAUI, Uno, WPF, WinUI, Blazor, ...)
- [ ] Rendering output / visual behavior
- [ ] Performance
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] Build, packaging, or CI
- [x] Documentation or samples

## Changes

None — this PR regenerates API-diff and release-note documentation from prepared release facts. The release-note prose describes existing shipped or planned product behavior and does not alter the public API or runtime behavior.

## Testing

Ran `python3 scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-render.py --all`, which validated the prose and rendered all 89 release-note pages plus the TOC and release index.

## Checklist

- [ ] Tests added or updated (not applicable: documentation-only regeneration)
- [x] `Changes` above lists all public API and behavioral changes (or "None.")
- [ ] New/changed public API? Added or updated accurate source `///` documentation and regenerated bindings when applicable (not applicable)
- [ ] Native change? Companion `mono/skia` PR linked above and bindings regenerated (not applicable)

[Azure Pipelines](https://azure.microsoft.com/services/devops/pipelines/) offers cloud-hosted pipelines for Linux, macOS, and Windows with 10 free parallel jobs and unlimited minutes for open source projects.

:v: **Any language, platform, and cloud**
Build, test, and deploy Node.js, Python,  Java, PHP, Ruby, Go, C/C++, C#, Android, and iOS apps. Run in parallel on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Deploy to cloud providers like Azure, AWS, and GCP. Distribute mobile apps through beta channels and app stores.

:whale2: **Native container support**
Create new containers with ease and push them to any registry. Deploy containers to independent hosts or Kubernetes.

:muscle: **Advanced workflows and features**
Easy build chaining and multi-phased builds. Support for YAML, test integration, release gates, reporting, and more.

:wrench: **Extensible**
Use a range of build, test, and deployment tasks built by the community – hundreds of extensions from Slack to SonarCloud. You can even deploy from other CI systems, like Jenkins. Webhooks and REST APIs help you integrate.

:blue_heart: **Free, to you from Azure Pipelines**
Free cloud-hosted builds for public and private repositories.

Ran `python3 scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-render.py --all` successfully to validate every prose file and regenerate all release pages, `TOC.yml`, and `index.md`.

[Azure Pipelines](https://azure.microsoft.com/services/devops/pipelines/) offers cloud-hosted pipelines for Linux, macOS, and Windows with 10 free parallel jobs and unlimited minutes for open source projects.

:v: **Any language, platform, and cloud**
Build, test, and deploy Node.js, Python,  Java, PHP, Ruby, Go, C/C++, C#, Android, and iOS apps. Run in parallel on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Deploy to cloud providers like Azure, AWS, and GCP. Distribute mobile apps through beta channels and app stores.

:whale2: **Native container support**
Create new containers with ease and push them to any registry. Deploy containers to independent hosts or Kubernetes.

:muscle: **Advanced workflows and features**
Easy build chaining and multi-phased builds. Support for YAML, test integration, release gates, reporting, and more.

:wrench: **Extensible**
Use a range of build, test, and deployment tasks built by the community – hundreds of extensions from Slack to SonarCloud. You can even deploy from other CI systems, like Jenkins. Webhooks and REST APIs help you integrate.

:blue_heart: **Free, to you from Azure Pipelines**
Free cloud-hosted builds for public and private repositories.

pr.title: [docs] docs: regenerate API diffs and release notes
pr.body:
## Description

Regenerates API diffs and release notes from the prepared release metadata. Adds reviewed consumer-facing prose for the 4.150 through 4.155 release lines, including m152 stable and m153/m154 preview migration guidance, then rebuilds the release-note index and TOC.

**Related issues**

None.

**Required skia PR**

None.

**Areas affected**

- [ ] Managed API (`binding/`)
- [ ] Native / C API (`externals/skia/src/c`, `include/c`)
- [ ] Generated P/Invoke bindings
- [ ] Native dependency or Skia update (libpng, HarfBuzz, FreeType, zlib, milestone bump, ...)
- [ ] Views & integrations (MAUI, Uno, WPF, WinUI, Blazor, ...)
- [ ] Rendering output / visual behavior
- [ ] Performance
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] Build, packaging, or CI
- [x] Documentation or samples

## Changes

None — regenerates release documentation and API-diff pages without changing the public API or runtime behavior.

## Testing

Ran `python3 scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-render.py --all` successfully, which validated the prose and rendered all 89 release-note pages plus the TOC and index.

## Checklist

- [ ] Tests added or updated (not applicable: documentation generation only)
- [x] `Changes` above lists all public API and behavioral changes (or "None.")
- [ ] New/changed public API? Added or updated accurate source `///` documentation and regenerated bindings when applicable
- [ ] Native change? Companion `mono/skia` PR linked above and bindings regenerated

[Azure Pipelines](https://azure.microsoft.com/services/devops/pipelines/) offers cloud-hosted pipelines for Linux, macOS, and Windows with 10 free parallel jobs and unlimited minutes for open source projects.

:v: **Any language, platform, and cloud**
Build, test, and deploy Node.js, Python,  Java, PHP, Ruby, Go, C/C++, C#, Android, and iOS apps. Run in parallel on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Deploy to cloud providers like Azure, AWS, and GCP. Distribute mobile apps through beta channels and app stores.

:whale2: **Native container support**
Create new containers with ease and push them to any registry. Deploy containers to independent hosts or Kubernetes.

:muscle: **Advanced workflows and features**
Easy build chaining and multi-phased builds. Support for YAML, test integration, release gates, reporting, and more.

:wrench: **Extensible**
Use a range of build, test, and deployment tasks built by the community – hundreds of extensions from Slack to SonarCloud. You can even deploy from other CI systems, like Jenkins. Webhooks and REST APIs help you integrate.

:blue_heart: **Free, to you from Azure Pipelines**
Free cloud-hosted builds for public and private repositories.

### Continuously build, test, and deploy to any platform and cloud

[Azure Pipelines](https://azure.microsoft.com/services/devops/pipelines/) offers cloud-hosted pipelines for Linux, macOS, and Windows with 10 free parallel jobs and unlimited minutes for open source projects.

:v: **Any language, platform, and cloud**
Build, test, and deploy Node.js, Python,  Java, PHP, Ruby, Go, C/C++, C#, Android, and iOS apps. Run in parallel on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Deploy to cloud providers like Azure, AWS, and GCP. Distribute mobile apps through beta channels and app stores.

:whale2: **Native container support**
Create new containers with ease and push them to any registry. Deploy containers to independent hosts or Kubernetes.

:muscle: **Advanced workflows and features**
Easy build chaining and multi-phased builds. Support for YAML, test integration, release gates, reporting, and more.

:wrench: **Extensible**
Use a range of build, test, and deployment tasks built by the community – hundreds of extensions from Slack to SonarCloud. You can even deploy from other CI systems, like Jenkins. Webhooks and REST APIs help you integrate.

:blue_heart: **Free, to you from Azure Pipelines**
Free cloud-hosted builds for public and private repositories.

...

app.name: Dotnet Policy Service
app.description:
The GitHub Policy Service is created and maintained by the GitHub Inside Microsoft team at Microsoft 1ES. This service is the foundation for the compliance and governance efforts on our GitHub instances. In a nutshell, the Policy Service manages GitHub organizations and repositories using Config-As-Code.

This instance is dedicated to the .NET Foundation and its projects.

Microsoft project maintainers who are employees can learn more about this app, including support and feedback opportunities, at [GitOps](https://aka.ms/1es-gitops).
For commands to interact with the bots you have to use @dotnet-policy-service.

repository.name: SkiaSharp
repository.description: SkiaSharp is a cross-platform 2D graphics API for .NET platforms based on Google's Skia Graphics Library. It provides a comprehensive 2D API that can be used across mobile, server and desktop models to render images.

pr.title: [docs] docs: regenerate API diffs and release notes
pr.body:
## Description

Regenerates the prepared 4.155.0 release-note facts and API-diff artifacts, then adds consumer-facing notes for restored Linux NoDependencies system-font discovery. The rendered release page and release index are kept in sync with the authoritative source JSON.

**Related issues**

None.

**Required skia PR**

None.

**Areas affected**

- [ ] Managed API (`binding/`)
- [ ] Native / C API (`externals/skia/src/c`, `include/c`)
- [ ] Generated P/Invoke bindings
- [ ] Native dependency or Skia update (libpng, HarfBuzz, FreeType, zlib, milestone bump, ...)
- [ ] Views & integrations (MAUI, Uno, WPF, WinUI, Blazor, ...)
- [ ] Rendering output / visual behavior
- [ ] Performance
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] Build, packaging, or CI
- [x] Documentation or samples

## Changes

None — documentation and generated API-diff/release-note artifacts only; no public API or runtime behavior changed by this PR.

## Testing

Ran `python3 scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-render.py documentation/docfx/releases/_sources/4.155.0-unreleased.data.json documentation/docfx/releases/_sources/4.155.0-unreleased.prose.json documentation/docfx/releases/4.155.0-unreleased.md`, then `python3 scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-render.py --all` successfully. No product tests were needed for documentation-only changes.

## Checklist

- [ ] Tests added or updated (not needed for documentation-only changes)
- [x] `Changes` above lists all public API and behavioral changes (or "None.")
- [ ] New/changed public API? Added or updated accurate source `///` documentation and regenerated bindings when applicable
- [ ] Native change? Companion `mono/skia` PR linked above and bindings regenerated

Create new containers with ease and push them to any registry. Deploy containers to independent hosts or Kubernetes.

:wrench: **Extensible**

:blue_heart: **Free, to you from Azure Pipelines**

The GitHub Policy Service is created and maintained by the GitHub Inside Microsoft team at Microsoft 1ES. This service is the foundation for the compliance and governance efforts on our GitHub instances. In a nutshell, the Policy Service manages GitHub organizations and repositories using Config-As-Code.

This instance is dedicated to the .NET Foundation and its projects.

Microsoft project maintainers who are employees can learn more about this app, including support and feedback opportunities, at [GitOps](https://aka.ms/1es-gitops).
For commands to interact with the bots you have to use @dotnet-policy-service.

pr.title: [docs] docs: regenerate API diffs and release notes
pr.body:
## Description

Regenerates the prepared release-note facts and API-diff inputs, and adds curated prose for the unreleased 4.155.0 page. The page highlights restored Linux NoDependencies system-font discovery and Tizen 10 GCC 14.2 packaging.

**Related issues**

None.

**Required skia PR**

None.

**Areas affected**

- [ ] Managed API (`binding/`)
- [ ] Native / C API (`externals/skia/src/c`, `include/c`)

The GitHub Policy Service is created and maintained by the GitHub Inside Microsoft team at Microsoft 1ES. This service is the foundation for the compliance and governance efforts on our GitHub instances. In a nutshell, the Policy Service manages GitHub organizations and repositories using Config-As-Code.

This instance is dedicated to the .NET Foundation and its projects.

Microsoft project maintainers who are employees can learn more about this app, including support and feedback opportunities, at [GitOps](https://aka.ms/1es-gitops).
For commands to interact with the bots you have to use @dotnet-policy-service.

pr.title: [docs] Regenerate API diffs and release notes
pr.body:
## Description

Regenerates the prepared 4.155.0 release-note facts and API-diff metadata, then adds consumer-facing prose for restored Linux NoDependencies system-font discovery and refreshed Tizen 10 native packages.

**Related issues**

None.

**Required skia PR**

None.

**Areas affected**

- [ ] Managed API (`binding/`)
- [ ] Native / C API (`externals/skia/src/c`, `include/c`)
- [ ] Generated P/Invoke bindings
- [ ] Native dependency or Skia update (libpng, HarfBuzz, FreeType, zlib, milestone bump, ...)
- [ ] Views & integrations (MAUI, Uno, WPF, WinUI, Blazor, ...)
- [ ] Rendering output / visual behavior
- [ ] Performance
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] Build, packaging, or CI
- [x] Documentation or samples

## Changes

None — documentation and generated release-note metadata only; no public API or runtime behavior changes.

## Testing

- Passed: `python3 scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-render.py documentation/docfx/releases/_sources/4.155.0-unreleased.data.json documentation/docfx/releases/_sources/4.155.0-unreleased.prose.json documentation/docfx/releases/4.155.0-unreleased.md`
- Passed: `python3 scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-render.py --all` (rendered 92 pages and rebuilt the release TOC/index)

## Checklist

- [ ] Tests added or updated (not applicable: documentation and generated metadata only)
- [x] `Changes` above lists all public API and behavioral changes (or "None.")

### Continuously build, test, and deploy to any platform and cloud

[Azure Pipelines](https://azure.microsoft.com/services/devops/pipelines/) offers cloud-hosted pipelines for Linux, macOS, and Windows with 10 free parallel jobs and unlimited minutes for open source projects.

:v: **Any language, platform, and cloud**
Build, test, and deploy Node.js, Python,  Java, PHP, Ruby, Go, C/C++, C#, Android, and iOS apps. Run in parallel on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Deploy to cloud providers like Azure, AWS, and GCP. Distribute mobile apps through beta channels and app stores.

:whale2: **Native container support**
Create new containers with ease and push them to any registry. Deploy containers to independent hosts or Kubernetes.

:muscle: **Advanced workflows and features**
Easy build chaining and multi-phased builds. Support for YAML, test integration, release gates, reporting, and more.

:wrench: **Extensible**
Use a range of build, test, and deployment tasks built by the community – hundreds of extensions from Slack to SonarCloud. You can even deploy from other CI systems, like Jenkins. Webhooks and REST APIs help you integrate.

:blue_heart: **Free, to you from Azure Pipelines**
Free cloud-hosted builds for public and private repositories.

...

[Azure Pipelines](https://azure.microsoft.com/services/devops/pipelines/) offers cloud-hosted pipelines for Linux, macOS, and Windows with 10 free parallel jobs and unlimited minutes for open source projects.

:v: **Any language, platform, and cloud**

:whale2: **Native container support**
Create new containers with ease and push them to any registry. Deploy containers to independent hosts or Kubernetes.

Easy build chaining and multi-phased builds. Support for YAML, test integration, release gates, reporting, and more.

:wrench: **Extensible**
Use a range of build, test, and deployment tasks built by the community – hundreds of extensions from Slack to SonarCloud. You can even deploy from other CI systems, like Jenkins. Webhooks and REST APIs help you integrate.

:blue_heart: **Free, to you from Azure Pipelines**
Free cloud-hosted builds for public and private repositories.

pr.title: [docs] docs: regenerate API diffs and release notes
pr.body:
## Description

Regenerates the prepared API-diff and release-note facts, then adds consumer-facing prose for the 4.155.0 unreleased page. This documents restored Linux NoDependencies system-font discovery, Tizen 10 packaging, and the m155 native fork cleanup.

**Related issues**

None.

**Required skia PR**

None.

**Areas affected**

- [ ] Managed API (`binding/`)
- [ ] Native / C API (`externals/skia/src/c`, `include/c`)
- [ ] Generated P/Invoke bindings
- [ ] Native dependency or Skia update (libpng, HarfBuzz, FreeType, zlib, milestone bump, ...)
- [ ] Views & integrations (MAUI, Uno, WPF, WinUI, Blazor, ...)
- [ ] Rendering output / visual behavior
- [ ] Performance
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] Build, packaging, or CI
- [x] Documentation or samples

## Changes

None — documentation and generated release-note/API-diff artifacts only; no public API or runtime behavior changes.

## Testing

Ran `python3 scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-render.py documentation/docfx/releases/_sources/4.155.0-unreleased.data.json documentation/docfx/releases/_sources/4.155.0-unreleased.prose.json documentation/docfx/releases/4.155.0-unreleased.md` and `python3 scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-render.py --all`. The final render validated and rebuilt all 92 pages plus the release TOC and index.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated (not applicable: documentation-only change; renderer validation run)
- [x] `Changes` above lists all public API and behavioral changes (or "None.")
- [ ] New/changed public API? Added or updated accurate source `///` documentation and regenerated bindings when applicable
- [ ] Native change? Companion `mono/skia` PR linked above and bindings regenerated

[Azure Pipelines](https://azure.microsoft.com/services/devops/pipelines/) offers cloud-hosted pipelines for Linux, macOS, and Windows with 10 free parallel jobs and unlimited minutes for open source projects.

:v: **Any language, platform, and cloud**
Build, test, and deploy Node.js, Python,  Java, PHP, Ruby, Go, C/C++, C#, Android, and iOS apps. Run in parallel on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Deploy to cloud providers like Azure, AWS, and GCP. Distribute mobile apps through beta channels and app stores.

:whale2: **Native container support**
Create new containers with ease and push them to any registry. Deploy containers to independent hosts or Kubernetes.

:muscle: **Advanced workflows and features**
Easy build chaining and multi-phased builds. Support for YAML, test integration, release gates, reporting, and more.

:wrench: **Extensible**
Use a range of build, test, and deployment tasks built by the community – hundreds of extensions from Slack to SonarCloud. You can even deploy from other CI systems, like Jenkins. Webhooks and REST APIs help you integrate.

:blue_heart: **Free, to you from Azure Pipelines**
Free cloud-hosted builds for public and private repositories.

pr.title: [docs] docs: regenerate API diffs and release notes
pr.body:
## Description

Regenerates the prepared API-diff and release-note data, adds reviewed prose for the unreleased 4.155.0 line, and renders the release-note site aggregates. The new page calls out restored Linux NoDependencies system-font discovery and the Tizen 10 native-asset platform floor.

**Related issues**

None.

**Required skia PR**

None.

**Areas affected**

- [ ] Managed API (`binding/`)
- [ ] Native / C API (`externals/skia/src/c`, `include/c`)
- [ ] Generated P/Invoke bindings
- [ ] Native dependency or Skia update (libpng, HarfBuzz, FreeType, zlib, milestone bump, ...)
- [ ] Views & integrations (MAUI, Uno, WPF, WinUI, Blazor, ...)
- [ ] Rendering output / visual behavior
- [ ] Performance
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] Build, packaging, or CI
- [x] Documentation or samples

## Changes

None — documentation generation and release-note prose only; no public API or runtime behavior changes.

## Testing

Ran `python3 scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-render.py documentation/docfx/releases/_sources/4.155.0-unreleased.data.json documentation/docfx/releases/_sources/4.155.0-unreleased.prose.json documentation/docfx/releases/4.155.0-unreleased.md` and `python3 scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-render.py --all`. Both completed successfully; the final render rebuilt 92 pages plus the release TOC and index.

## Checklist

- [ ] Tests added or updated (not applicable: documentation-generation change only)
- [x] `Changes` above lists all public API and behavioral changes (or "None.")
- [ ] New/changed public API? Added or updated accurate source `///` documentation and regenerated bindings when applicable
- [ ] Native change? Companion `mono/skia` PR linked above and bindings regenerated

content.title: [aw] Failed jobs: Documentation Bot
content.body:
### Failed Jobs in Workflow Run

**Workflow:** [Documentation Bot](https://github.com/vaadin/flow/blob/main/.github/workflows/doc-bot.md)  
**Run:** https://github.com/vaadin/flow/actions/runs/35074832704

The following jobs failed in this workflow run:

- [`safe_outputs`](https://github.com/vaadin/flow/actions/runs/35074832704/job/104727108102)


<!-- gh-aw-agentic-workflow: Documentation Bot, id: 35074832704, run: https://github.com/vaadin/flow/actions/runs/35074832704 -->
> - [x] expires <!-- gh-aw-expires: 2026-09-23T08:49:24.256Z --> on Sep 23, 2026, 8:49 AM UTC
content.author: github-actions[bot]

comments.body:
## What failed

Run [35074832704](https://github.com/vaadin/flow/actions/runs/35074832704) of the Documentation Bot: the `agent` job succeeded and the documentation pull request was created (vaadin/docs#6048), but the `safe_outputs` job failed on the next message:

```
Assigning 1 users to issue #25750 in vaadin/docs: ["totally-not-ai[bot]"]
POST /repos/vaadin/docs/issues/25750/assignees - 404
Failed to assign users: Not Found
✗ Message 2 (assign_to_user) failed
```

This is a real bug in `.github/workflows/doc-bot.md`, not a transient CI problem. It will fail on every run that opens a documentation pull request.

## Root cause

`assign_to_user` is configured with `target-repo: "vaadin/docs"`, so the number it is given is resolved against `vaadin/docs`. The agent emitted:

```json
{"type":"assign_to_user","assignee":"totally-not-ai[bot]","issue_number":"25750", ...}
```

`25750` is the **Flow** pull request number. `vaadin/docs` has no item with that number, so the POST 404s and the failed message fails the job.

The agent is not doing anything unreasonable — the prompt asks for something it cannot do. Phase 5a says *"Then assign the new pull request to `@PR_AUTHOR` with the `assign-to-user` safe-output"*, but the documentation pull request does not exist while the agent runs: it is opened afterwards, by the `create_pull_request` safe-output, from the agent's own output. The only number the agent has is the Flow one, so that is what it filled in.

Passing a `temporary_id` reference instead would not help either: `assign_to_user` reads the number through a plain `parseInt` and never consults the resolved temporary-id map, so `#aw_xxx` fails there as an invalid number (still true in the current gh-aw release).

Two smaller things fall out of the same cause:

1. The assignee is an app account (`totally-not-ai[bot]`, which is on the workflow's `bots:` allow list, so this is a normal case). App accounts cannot be issue assignees, so this assignment could not have succeeded even with the right number.
2. Phase 6 has the same missing-number problem, without failing the run. The comment template is `vaadin/docs#<NUMBER>`, and the agent posted *"a draft documentation pull request … has been opened on branch `doc-bot/vaadin-flow/25750` (the exact PR number isn't visible from this run)"* — so the comment on the source pull request does not link the documentation pull request.

## Proposed fix

Assign from the safe-output that opens the pull request, which is the first thing that knows its number, and drop `assign-to-user` entirely:

```yaml
create-pull-request:
  target-repo: "vaadin/docs"
  ...
  assignees: ["${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}"]
```

`create-pull-request` applies these after creating the pull request, against the right repository and number, and logs a warning instead of failing when a user cannot be assigned — which is the behaviour the prompt already describes ("this is not a failure"). That covers the app-account case too.

For the comment, give the create output a `temporary_id` and reference it in the comment body. `add-comment` does resolve temporary ids in `body`, and cross-repository references are rendered as `vaadin/docs#<NUMBER>`, so the comment links the real pull request instead of saying the number is unavailable.

A draft pull request with this change is on the way from branch `ci/doc-bot-assign-docs-pr-at-creation`. It is workflow-only: `doc-bot.md` plus the recompiled `doc-bot.lock.yml` (compiled with the same gh-aw v0.86.2 the lock file already records, so the diff is limited to the change).

## Separate finding, not fixed here

Phase 0 detects an existing documentation pull request with:

```bash
git -C docs-repo rev-parse --verify "origin/doc-bot/vaadin-flow/${PR_NUMBER}"
```

That ref never exists. `create-pull-request` salts the branch name — `Using branch name from JSONL with added salt: doc-bot/vaadin-flow/25750-1e760aff0c31c524` — and the branches in `vaadin/docs` confirm it (`doc-bot/vaadin-flow/25724-…`, `…/25730-…`, `…/24484-…`). So the "update the existing pull request" path (Phase 5b) can never be taken, and a re-run opens a second documentation pull request for the same source pull request instead of updating the first.

Since the workflow now runs once per merge, with `cancel-in-progress`, this mostly affects manual re-runs. Two ways to fix it, both a behaviour change that seems worth a decision rather than folding into this one:

- Set `preserve-branch-name: true` on `create-pull-request`, so the branch is exactly the name Phase 0 looks for.
- Or have Phase 0 match `origin/doc-bot/vaadin-flow/${PR_NUMBER}-*` as well and pass the branch it finds to Phase 5b.

@mshabarov you own this workflow — the fix above is the narrow one for the failing job; the branch-name question is yours to call.
